jobs.excerpt: About OpenSesameOpenSesame is transforming workforce development with an AI-powered marketplace of skill-building courses and learning pathways.
jobs.description:
About OpenSesame

OpenSesame is transforming workforce development with an AI-powered marketplace of skill-building courses and learning pathways. We help organizations build skills and stay compliant through a high-quality content catalog, seamless LMS/LXP integrations, and advanced capabilities like skills-based curation and multilingual content creation. More than 2,000 companies, including 150+ of the Global 2000, rely on OpenSesame to develop the world's most productive and admired workforces.

Learn more: www.opensesame.com/about

About the Team

The Partnerships team builds and scales OpenSesame's global partner ecosystem. We work across technology, channel, referral, reseller, marketplace, and strategic alliances to expand reach of our joint solutions and deliver exceptional experiences for our partners and their customers.

The Strategic Partner Manager (SPM) is the relationship owner responsible for driving revenue growth, partner activation, and strategic alignment with assigned partners. SPMs operate within a system designed for partner success—they maintain consistent cadences, deliver quick wins, build trust, and drive pipeline behavior. Through partner planning, enablement, and execution, SPMs translate company strategy into partner-led revenue.

About the Role

OpenSesame is seeking an entrepreneurial, relationship-focused Strategic Partner Manager to own a portfolio of strategic partners, drive sourced and influenced revenue, and deliver consistent partner value.

As an SPM, you will manage a book of partner relationships, each with its own business model, sales structure, and growth opportunity. You'll partner with Marketing, Sales, Product, and Operations to activate partners, create joint go-to-market motions, and drive pipeline. This is a blend of relationship management, commercial acumen, strategic thinking, and execution—combining partner business planning with day-to-day touchpoints that keep partners engaged and accountable.

What You'll Do

Know & Own Your Partner Portfolio

You are the primary expert and relationship owner on/for your assigned partners. You segment and prioritize partners based on strategic potential, current performance, partner health, and market opportunity and identify when a partnership should be accelerated, remediated, restructured, or deprioritized. You maintain consistent touchpoints (weekly/bi-weekly), drive quarterly business reviews (QBRs), align on joint strategies, and keep partners accountable to their OpenSesame revenue targets. You build trust through reliability and genuine enthusiasm for partner success.

Drive Pipeline & Revenue

You own sourced and influenced pipeline and booking targets for your partner portfolio. You work with partners to identify co-sell opportunities, activate referral channels, and expand OEM relationships. You maintain pipeline visibility, align with Sales on shared opportunities, and work with partners to move deals forward.

Plan & Execute Partner Growth

You identify opportunities to expand the scope and value of your partnerships by understanding each partner’s strategy, customer base, sales motion, product roadmap, and economics. You evaluate new routes to market, commercial models, integrations, and joint offerings, then align stakeholders and drive the highest-potential opportunities from idea through execution. You develop partner business plans that outline quarterly targets, go-to-market motions, campaign priorities, and success metrics. You coordinate with Partner Marketing to execute co-marketing campaigns, sales plays, and enablement activities. You use planning frameworks and tools (Euler, Crossbeam, Salesforce, Gong) to drive accountability and measure progress.

Enable & Activate Partners

You ensure partners have the content, messaging, demos, training, and certifications they need to effectively sell and support OpenSesame. You equip partners to understand OpenSesame’s value proposition, confidently position our solutions, and generate pipeline in alignment with OpenSesame sales teams and GTM priorities. Using Highspot and other enablement tools, you coordinate partner onboarding, training, and ongoing enablement while reinforcing best practices that improve partner effectiveness, sales alignment, and operational efficiency.

Be a Strategic Partner Internally

You represent your partners internally. You escalate integration requests, coordinate with Product and Support for critical issues, align Sales on shared accounts, and surface insights that help OpenSesame serve partners better. You maintain visibility into partner technical contacts and ensure proper escalation paths during critical issues.

Performance Objectives

First 30 Days: Learn & Align

Build a strong understanding of OpenSesame's partner ecosystem, your assigned partner portfolio, and how you'll succeed in this role.

Success looks like:

  • Complete OpenSesame onboarding, partner playbook training, and system access (Salesforce, Highspot, Crossbeam, Euler, Gong)
  • Introduce yourself to each partner in your portfolio and schedule recurring touchpoints
  • Understand each partner's business model, OpenSesame integrations, current pipeline, key contacts, and the relevant technology and SaaS context needed to effectively manage the portfolio.
  • Meet with your SPM team, manager, and cross-functional stakeholders (Marketing, Sales, Product, Operations)
  • Align with leadership on expectations, goals, and your plan for the first 90 days

Days 30–90: Build Relationships & Demonstrate Impact

Establish yourself as a trusted partner by delivering quick wins, maintaining consistency, and driving early revenue momentum.

Success looks like:

  • Develop a business plan for each partner, including quarterly targets, key initiatives, and success metrics
  • Schedule and conduct first QBRs with each partner, establishing alignment and cadence
  • Maintain weekly/bi-weekly touchpoints and respond quickly to partner requests
  • Coordinate one partner marketing campaign or enablement initiative
  • Present an assessment of your partner portfolio, including early wins and challenges

Days 90–120: Drive Pipeline & Optimize Execution

Demonstrate consistent progress toward quarterly targets while identifying opportunities to improve partner execution and OpenSesame alignment.

Success looks like:

  • Maintain pipeline visibility and pacing toward quarterly revenue targets
  • Keep partners engaged through consistent communication, quick wins, and clear next steps
  • Identify operational or program friction points and surface recommendations for improvement
  • Build relationships with key technical and commercial contacts at strategic partners

Months 4–12: Mature Partnerships & Drive Sustained Growth

Lead mature, predictable partnerships that consistently generate sourced and influenced revenue while exploring opportunities for deeper strategic collaboration.

Success looks like:

  • Consistently meet or exceed quarterly targets (sourced and influenced)
  • Maintain partner health through regular QBRs, strategic planning, and alignment on joint goals
  • Proactively identify and solve partner challenges before they impact trust or revenue
  • Lead strategic initiatives that deepen partner relationships (e.g., joint roadmap planning, co-marketing)
  • Be recognized as a trusted partner across OpenSesame (Sales, Marketing, Product, Operations)

What Success Looks Like

  • Partners consistently generate meaningful sourced and influenced revenue.
  • Your partners are engaged, responsive, and aligned on OpenSesame's positioning and value.
  • You maintain pipeline visibility and demonstrate pacing toward targets.
  • Cadence matters—your partners expect consistent touchpoints and know what to expect from you.
  • Relationships run deep—key partner contacts trust you, advocate for you, and come to you with opportunities.
  • You're a trusted partner internally—Sales, Marketing, and Product come to you for partner insights.

Travel Requirement: This role may require up to 20% travel based on business needs, including company meetings, partner engagements, and other activities.

Location: This position can be located anywhere in the U.S. In addition to position-specific travel requirements, all positions will require up to 15 days of travel per year for company-wide events (typically January, May, September).

Performance Driven: We’re looking for self-starters with a track record of follow-through, curiosity, and results. We don’t hire based on a checklist — we hire for potential, drive, and evidence of performance. If you’re motivated to learn, comfortable with experimentation, and excited about how technology can make sales more human, you’ll fit right in.

Compensation: The base salary for this position typically ranges from $120,000 to $145,000 USD annually, depending on experience and level. This role is also eligible for up to a 30% bonus. We carefully consider a wide range of compensation factors, relying on market data to determine compensation and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience.

Full-Time | Remote | Flexible U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Go-to-Market (GTM) Lead to own the strategy and hands-on execution of two upcoming B2B SaaS product launches.

This is not a coordination-only role. As the first GTM hire, you’ll build the go-to-market motion from the ground up — from positioning and messaging to beta acquisition, launch campaigns, demand generation, and repeatable GTM playbooks.

You’ll work directly with leadership in an early-stage startup environment where speed, experimentation, and ownership matter.

If you’ve launched B2B SaaS products before, thrive in ambiguity, and enjoy building from zero, this role is for you.

What You’ll Own

B2B SaaS Go-to-Market & Product Launch

  • Own end-to-end GTM strategy and execution for two SaaS products
  • Build launch plans covering:
    • Positioning and messaging
    • Target audiences
    • Distribution
    • User acquisition
    • Demand generation
    • Launch campaigns
  • Personally execute GTM initiatives rather than simply managing them
  • Use insights from the first product launch to improve the second
  • Rapidly test, learn, and iterate based on market response

Beta User Acquisition

  • Identify and recruit qualified beta users and early adopters
  • Build and execute creative outbound and acquisition campaigns
  • Engage directly with prospective users
  • Develop relationships with early adopters and collect structured feedback
  • Turn user insights into improvements across messaging, targeting, and launch strategy
  • Drive early adoption and product engagement

Positioning, Messaging & Copywriting

  • Develop clear positioning for each SaaS product
  • Translate product capabilities into compelling customer value propositions
  • Build messaging around:
    • Customer pain points
    • Use cases
    • Differentiation
    • Business outcomes
  • Write high-converting copy for landing pages, emails, outreach, and launch campaigns
  • Continuously refine messaging based on customer feedback and performance data

Demand Generation & Launch Campaigns

  • Build and execute campaigns that generate awareness, users, and pipeline
  • Create:
    • Landing pages
    • Email campaigns
    • Outreach sequences
    • User onboarding flows
    • Launch materials
  • Test different channels, audiences, offers, and messaging
  • Track funnel performance and identify opportunities to improve conversion
  • Coordinate with leadership and other stakeholders to keep launches moving quickly

GTM Systems & Playbooks

  • Build GTM infrastructure from scratch
  • Document:
    • Launch processes
    • Outreach workflows
    • Messaging frameworks
    • Experiments
    • Performance insights
    • Lessons learned
  • Turn successful experiments into repeatable processes
  • Build scalable playbooks that can support future product launches

Required Experience & Skills

  • 4–8 years of experience across:
    • Go-to-Market
    • Product Marketing
    • Growth Marketing
    • Demand Generation
  • Proven experience launching at least one B2B SaaS product end-to-end
  • Experience working as an early GTM hire or in an early-stage startup environment
  • Strong understanding of SaaS positioning, messaging, and customer acquisition
  • Excellent copywriting and conversion-focused messaging skills
  • Hands-on experience executing:
    • Outreach campaigns
    • Demand generation
    • Product launches
    • User acquisition
  • Ability to build processes and systems from scratch
  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to learn from campaign and user data
  • Comfortable working independently with minimal structure

Nice to Have

  • Experience as an employee #1–5 GTM hire
  • Early-stage B2B SaaS startup experience
  • Product-led growth experience
  • Experience running beta or early-access programs
  • Founder-led marketing exposure
  • Familiarity with:
    • CRM platforms
    • Marketing automation
    • Email marketing platforms
    • Landing page builders
  • Experience developing repeatable GTM playbooks across multiple launches

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You’ve actually launched SaaS products, not just supported launches
  • You can move from strategy to execution without waiting for another team
  • You’re comfortable building when there is no existing playbook
  • You move quickly and iterate based on real customer feedback
  • You’re equally comfortable writing messaging, recruiting beta users, launching campaigns, and analyzing results
  • You thrive in high-ownership startup environments
  • You care more about measurable outcomes than activity

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day could start by reviewing beta acquisition and launch funnel performance, followed by refining product messaging based on user feedback.

You might then build a new outreach sequence, improve a landing page, recruit beta users, analyze campaign conversion rates, and work with leadership on the next launch experiment.

You’ll also document what worked, what didn’t, and how those learnings should influence the next campaign or product launch.

In short: you take B2B SaaS products from pre-launch to market by owning positioning, acquisition, execution, experimentation, and growth.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Qualified beta users acquired
  • Beta activation and engagement
  • Launch funnel conversion rates
  • Pipeline and demand generated

  • Speed of GTM experimentation and execution

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Own launches across multiple B2B SaaS products
  • High autonomy over experimentation and execution
  • Opportunity to shape positioning, acquisition, and growth strategy
  • Growth potential into Head of Growth, Product Marketing Lead, or GTM Director

Interview Process

  2. Spark Hire Intro Video
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  4. Client Interview with Marketing Leadership
  5. Offer & Onboarding

Apply Now

If you’ve successfully launched B2B SaaS products, know how to acquire early users, and thrive when building GTM systems from scratch, we’d love to hear from you.

Join a fast-moving startup environment where you’ll have direct ownership over how new products enter the market and grow.

Future Group is not your traditional financial services company – we're a collective of super funds and services committed to changing our planet now for a better tomorrow. The role exists to support the Trustee in fulfilling its fiduciary, regulatory, and operational oversight responsibilities across superannuation administration, claims, complaints, and member outcomes. The role helps ensure strong governance and control over incidents, breaches and complaints; fair, consistent and compliant decision-making on claims and member matters; effective oversight of service providers; and continuous improvement in member outcomes, processes and disclosures. Future Group values diverse lived experience and identities, and we strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander backgrounds, those with caring responsibilities, from culturally and racially marginalised groups, with disabilities, who experience ageism, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and those who face social exclusion due to their social class.

Working as part of a broader Fund Operations team, you’ll provide cross-functional support across claims, complaints, incidents and remediation, service-provider and contact centre oversight, and member servicing.

You’ll help triage and resolve incidents and complaints, review claims and member matters within delegated authority, oversee service-provider performance, and support operational governance, risk and regulatory activities. You’ll also use insights from claims, complaints and member feedback to identify opportunities to improve processes, systems, disclosures and member outcomes.

You'll love this job if

  • You love sharing your ideas and seeing what happens. At this scale-up, you're not just a small fish in a big pond. Your contributions have a direct influence on our impact and how we work
  • You like to be kept on your toes - change is inevitable here. You like to tackle new challenges, and maybe even discover talents you never knew you had

  • You bring high attention to detail, sound judgment and problem-solving skills, can manage multiple priority tasks concurrently, and are willing to learn new skills and take on additional responsibilities
  • You’re also able to build strong, positive relationships with service providers, colleagues, Senior Leadership and the Office of the Superannuation Trustee, and can own and amicably resolve most escalations

  • Experience working with outsourced service providers

  • A B Corp organisation that cares about how it behaves inside and out

The groups are a safe, supportive space for people to share experiences and ideas

SPRCHRGR (pronounced "supercharger") is a professional services consultancy providing highly skilled team members across a variety of complementary disciplines. We like to say, “cut out the vowels, get there faster!” because we prioritize creativity, efficiency, and performance in our work, and we have fun doing it.

Our exceptional staff + innovative approach set us apart from stuffy traditional accountancies and commoditized outsourced bookkeeping agencies. We think differently about our work supporting high-growth startups, forward-thinking SMBs, and nonprofits located all across the US.

We specialize in cutting-edge technology and partner with dynamic businesses across diverse industries. Our team culture emphasizes collaboration, learning, and process-driven efficiency.

We're looking for someone who reads a trial balance and writes software. You'll build the client-facing financial tools for our fractional CFO firm: interactive dashboards and forecasting models, AI assistants that answer finance questions from live accounting data, and automations that take real recurring work off our clients' plates. We're small, we move fast, and we build our own tools instead of buying and configuring someone else's platform.

Who we are

SPRCHRGR combines executive financial leadership, fractional CFO work and controllership with data, systems integration and workflow automation. Our clients run $1 million to $50 million in revenue and get a white-glove build, not a template. We're small, we move fast, and we build our own tools (when it makes sense) instead of buying and configuring someone else's platform.

What you'll do

  • Build and own our client dashboards. Interactive financial models delivered as web apps, with scenario sliders, drill-down tables, and Excel exports a client's own finance lead can audit.
  • Build AI automations. Small, versioned automations that do one job properly, like turning a client's billing spreadsheet into reconciled QuickBooks invoices with built-in approval gates.
  • Get the data in yourself. Write the database queries behind our reporting and connect them to live client accounting data. Our VP of Technology owns the platform and will hand you the tools and procedures to work independently, not a ticket queue.
  • Be the person we trust when two numbers disagree. Work discrepancies to a documented answer, and know a genuine variance from two figures that were never comparable.
  • Teach the rest of us. Help our accountants and operators build their own tools instead of depending on you for every one.
  • Work directly with clients. Meet (virtually) with key client stakeholders to work out what they need, then build it. No layer in between, although you'll have full access to collaborate with other accounting + finance experts within our firm.

Who you are

You have both halves. Finance + Engineering.

  • Finance: real depth in accounting, financial statements, month-end close, receivables and payables, reconciliation, how a general ledger actually works. CPA or CMA is a strong signal; demonstrated judgment matters more.
  • Building: you write and maintain real code and real database queries. Our VP of Engineering partners with you to architect, maintain, and enhance the secure data warehouses, APIs, and hosted web app platform underneath. You can take a system with wrong or missing documentation, work out what it actually does, and build against reality. You've built AI tools, not just used them.

Minimum requirements

  • Bachelor's degree with a focus in Accounting, Finance, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of combined experience across accounting or finance and software or systems development.
  • CPA or CMA preferred, not required.
  • Proficiency in SQL preferred, not required.
  • Experience with at least one accounting system in depth, such as QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, or Dynamics.
  • Clear and concise communication, both written and verbal.
  • Comfortable working independently in a fully remote environment.
  • A dedicated workspace and access to reliable, secure, high-speed internet.
  • An unwavering commitment to confidentiality.
  • Based in the United States
  • Embrace SPRCHRGR's Core Values.

What this job isn't

  • Not a reporting role. If you just want to produce monthly financial packages, this is the wrong job.
  • Not a coordinator between finance and engineering. You build.
  • Not a management role in year one.
  • Not a place to learn accounting on the job.

Compensation and benefits

  • Fully Remote: Work from home with a structured schedule.
  • Career Growth: Gain hands-on mentoring and opportunities to work directly with our Founder & CEO.
  • Team-Oriented Environment: Collaborate with Software Engineers, Sr. Controllers, CFOs, and Accounting Managers to synthesize bespoke solutions for our clients.
  • Competitive pay: $150,000 - $180,000 Base Salary, DOE.
  • Phantom Equity: Eligible for consideration after your first year.
  • Bonus: Annual performance-based bonus compensation plan.
  • 401k: Up to a 4% match and no vesting period.
  • Benefits: Customizable options.

What will make you stand out

Send us something you built: a repository, a working file, or a written account of an automation you shipped end to end, with the before-and-after time it took. That matters more to us than a cover letter. If your best example is client work you can't share, tell us what it did and how you'd rebuild it!

At SPRCHRGR, we value fairness, clarity, and attention to detail in our hiring process. To ensure an equitable process, we ask that you submit your application only through the official posting for this role.

Ethical

We do good. We act with integrity, earning trust instead of asking for it, and we do what is right even when it isn’t easy. We are transparent, promptly sharing information and feedback directly and freely with all relevant stakeholders.

We love what we do. It shows in the positive and constructive attitude we bring every day. We realize work is more than just output; it’s about the life experiences we share along the way.

Job Summary and Purpose:

The Senior Program Manager – Global R&D Tax Credits & Business Analytics is responsible for the end-to-end leadership, execution, and expansion of Precision for Medicine's global R&D tax credit and innovation incentive programs.

This role serves as the business owner of the program, partnering with Finance, Tax, Operations, Clinical Development, Data Sciences, and country leadership teams to maximize available incentives while ensuring compliance, audit readiness, and operational efficiency.

The position will also lead strategic initiatives focused on analytics, reporting, process improvement, and business transformation across the organization. The successful candidate will combine expertise in R&D tax incentives with strong program management, business analytics, and stakeholder management skills.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Global R&D Tax Credit Program Ownership
    • Own Precision's global R&D tax credit program and related innovation incentive initiatives.
    • Develop and execute annual filing strategies and compliance plans across all participating countries.
    • Partner with business leaders to identify qualifying R&D activities and maximize eligible claims.
    • Coordinate documentation, financial support, technical narratives, and advisor deliverables.
    • Manage external tax advisors, consultants, auditors, and government agencies.
    • Lead responses to tax authority reviews, audits, and information requests.
    • Track legislative and regulatory developments impacting available incentives.
    • Maintain governance, documentation standards, controls, and audit readiness.

  • Global Expansion & Strategy

    • Identify and evaluate new country opportunities for R&D tax incentives, grants, and innovation funding programs.
    • Develop business cases supporting expansion into new jurisdictions.
    • Build scalable processes, templates, and governance structures to support global growth.
    • Partner with regional finance and operational leaders to launch and manage new programs.
    • Provide strategic recommendations to executive leadership regarding incentive opportunities and risks.

  • Financial Analysis & Business Intelligence

    • Develop KPI frameworks and reporting to measure program effectiveness and financial impact.
    • Partner with data and analytics teams to automate reporting and improve data quality.
    • Perform financial modeling, forecasting, and benefit realization analysis.
    • Create executive-level dashboards and presentations supporting decision making.
    • Identify opportunities for process automation and operational efficiencies.

  • Business Analytics & Transformation Initiatives

    • Support cross-functional projects involving analytics, reporting, master data, process improvement, automation, and operational excellence.
    • Partner with Finance, IT, HR, Clinical Operations, and Business Operations teams on enterprise initiatives.
    • Support development of self-service reporting and KPI governance frameworks.
    • Contribute to broader Finance and Analytics transformation efforts across Precision.

Education and Experience:

Minimum Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, Life Sciences, Engineering, or related field.
  • Experience within life sciences, CRO, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or professional services environments.
  • 7+ years of experience in R&D tax credits, government incentives, grants, finance, analytics, consulting, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex global programs involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Strong financial analysis, business analysis, and project management skills.
  • Experience working with international business teams and external advisors.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint proficiency.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical and financial concepts to non-technical audiences.

Preferred Education & Experience (optional):

  • MBA, CPA, MST, PMP, PhD, or equivalent advanced qualification.
  • Experience within life sciences, CRO, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or professional services environments.
  • Experience with international R&D incentive programs, grants, and innovation funding mechanisms.
  • Experience with Power BI, data visualization, and business intelligence platforms.
  • Experience supporting data governance, analytics, or business transformation initiatives.
  • Or equivalent combination of education, professional training and experience that provides the individual with the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the job.

Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:

  • Strategic thinker with strong business acumen.
  • Exceptional organizational and project management skills.
  • Ability to influence without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Highly self-motivated and able to work independently.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on operational excellence.

About MD Integrations

At MD Integrations, we partner with digital health brands to power clinical care at scale. We specialize in men's and women’s health, dermatology, endocrinology, and weight management, offering telehealth solutions that help patients receive expert, personalized care—all from the comfort of their home. Join our team and be part of the movement to make specialty care more accessible and impactful.

We are seeking a Senior HR Generalist with an emphasis in talent management to provide hands-on tactical ownership with strategic support as we scale. You'll partner with managers and employees across the organization to support their goals, coach managers through the fundamentals of people leadership, and drive full-cycle recruitment to secure best-in-class talent.

Overview

The Sr. HRG partners with managers and directors providing consultative support across talent management, workforce planning, legal and compliance, and employee relations. You will also help employees navigate all things employment from questions on benefits and pay to guiding them through a leave of absence. This role is critical to executing our people strategy daily, building trusted relationships, and coaching people leaders to success.

Partnering with our SVP, People you’ll function across core HR Operations and talent acquisition, while supporting the buildout of initiatives like performance and compensation frameworks, employee engagement and recognition programs, and learning and development strategies as the company grows.

Are you a business- and people-focused builder who thrives at the intersection of people and processes? Dive into the deep end and let us know if this sounds like you:

Key Responsibilities

  1. Coach and advise managers and directors, from first-time leaders to seasoned pros, through employee relations and organizational challenges to find practical, win-win outcomes benefiting the business and employees.
  2. Be the go-to, no-question-too-small resource for employees' everyday HR needs, from onboarding and offboarding to comp/benefits questions and the occasional LOA.
  3. Recruit top talent across the business in close partnership with hiring managers, from job design through the candidate experience. Immediate focus is on engineering and clinical operations roles, expanding to Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success over time.
  4. Own ongoing compliance for federal, state, and local employment law, leveraging Rippling ASO resources for multi-state requirements and policy updates.
  5. Support and lead change management initiatives that champion a people-first culture, including thoughtful planning, communication and implementation, minding the impact.
  6. Partner with the SVP to roll out and maintain new HR programs, including performance management and compensation frameworks, providing hands-on input and change management.
  7. Manage routine HCM administration, including data hygiene, employee records, time & attendance, and basic to intermediate reporting.
  8. Assess department talent needs and gaps to ensure teams have the right people, level and roles to meet objectives, using job design and talent attraction strategies to close them.
  9. Build scalable HR processes and documentation as we grow: see it, own it, make it better, then turn it into a how-to guide for easy use and distribution.
  10. Support payroll as backup to Accounting, partner on the annual comp review process, and keep employee changes (promotions, raises, role changes) accurately reflected in the HCM.

Your Work DNA

  • Entrepreneurial and ambitious, with a strong sense of initiative, ownership, and accountability.
  • Comfortable working with cross-functional teams across multiple time zones.
  • Customer-focused, responsive, and timely.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills, including active listening and sensitivity to individual needs.
  • Communicates effectively with people of diverse backgrounds and levels, inside and outside the organization.
  • Passionate about innovative HR solutions and process improvement in a (mildly) chaotic, fast-paced environment.

Qualifications

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in a mid-level HR Generalist, HR Business Partner, or Talent role with demonstrated ownership of meaningful scope (this is not an entry point for HR Coordinators or Assistants); we're looking for someone equally strong as an HR pro and recruiter.
  • Strong HR domain knowledge and business acumen, including familiarity with federal, state, and local labor laws (FMLA, ADA, etc.); HIPAA familiarity a plus.
  • Proven experience (and genuine enthusiasm for) recruiting professional-level roles; experience in Engineering and Clinical Ops (RN, MA, etc.) recruitment preferred, with the ability to flex into other functions like Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success as our hiring needs expand.
  • Strong background in talent management, job design, job descriptions, and recruitment; compensation expertise is a plus.
  • Proven experience leading people through growth-oriented organizational change, balancing evolving business needs with an employee-first, remote culture.
  • Thrives in a fast-growing, fully remote environment. Able to flex and reprioritize quickly across competing demands and tight timelines without losing momentum. Focus and personal accountability are a must-have.
  • Experience leveraging data and People analytics to generate insights and support business decisions is a nice to have, and something we’ll build upon as we grow.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule as workload demands (generally Monday–Friday).
  • Core tools: Rippling (HCM, ASO, Benefits broker), GSuite (Docs, Sheets, Meet, Drive), Slack, Asana (PM), AI tools for business.

What We Offer

  • Competitive Salary: Targeted range for this position is $75,000 - $95,000 per year DOE with opportunity to increase over time.
  • Comprehensive Benefits Package: Our benefits package includes 75% subsidized health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, paid time off, and a 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match.

jobs.description:
Sales Development Representative (SDR)

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Location: Remote (Open to LATAM & Global Candidates)
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours (CST)

About the Role

We are seeking a motivated and energetic Sales Development Representative (SDR) to join our growing team. In this role, you will be responsible for conducting high-volume outbound prospecting to identify and qualify leads across various sales campaigns.

The ideal candidate is a confident communicator who enjoys speaking with people, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and remains resilient when facing rejection. You will play a critical role in generating opportunities, qualifying prospects, and moving leads through the sales pipeline while delivering an exceptional experience throughout the process.

If you’re coachable, goal-oriented, and looking to build a successful career in sales, we’d love to hear from you.

Responsibilities

Outbound Prospecting

  • Conduct high-volume outbound outreach via phone, email, and text messaging.
  • Identify and engage prospective candidates and leads for assigned campaigns.
  • Build rapport quickly and maintain professional conversations with prospects.
  • Follow structured outreach cadences and prospecting workflows.
  • Consistently meet daily outreach activity goals.

Lead Qualification

  • Qualify prospects based on predefined campaign criteria.
  • Conduct discovery conversations to assess fit and interest.
  • Gather relevant information and identify next steps.
  • Advance qualified leads through the sales pipeline.
  • Ensure prospects receive a positive and professional experience.

Inbound Lead Follow-Up

  • Follow up with inbound leads generated through job postings and outreach efforts.
  • Engage interested prospects promptly and professionally.
  • Conduct qualification conversations and determine next steps.
  • Maintain communication with leads until a clear outcome is reached.

CRM & Pipeline Management

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all prospect interactions.
  • Log call notes, outreach activities, and lead status updates.
  • Track conversations and follow-up activities effectively.
  • Ensure CRM and tracking systems remain organized and accurate.
  • Support reporting efforts through detailed activity tracking.

Team Collaboration

  • Coordinate handoffs of qualified prospects to recruiting teams or sales leadership.
  • Communicate prospect insights and relevant information to stakeholders.
  • Participate in team meetings, coaching sessions, and training initiatives.
  • Collaborate with leadership to improve outreach effectiveness and campaign results.

Performance & Target Achievement

  • Meet daily and weekly outreach volume goals.
  • Achieve qualification and conversion targets.
  • Follow established sales processes and scripts.
  • Continuously improve outreach techniques and communication skills.
  • Maintain consistent activity and performance standards.

What Makes You a Perfect Fit?

  • High energy and enthusiasm.
  • Naturally personable and comfortable speaking with new people.
  • Strong resilience and ability to handle rejection professionally.
  • Goal-oriented and motivated by achieving results.
  • Highly organized with strong follow-up skills.
  • Coachable and eager to learn.
  • Strong work ethic and personal accountability.
  • Positive attitude and team-first mentality.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment.

Required Experience & Skills (Minimum)

  • Strong spoken and written English communication skills.
  • Ability to communicate confidently, clearly, and persuasively.
  • Comfortable making high-volume outbound calls.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple conversations and follow-up tasks simultaneously.
  • Ability to follow structured sales processes and scripts.
  • Reliable internet connection and dedicated remote workspace.
  • Availability to work during U.S. Central Standard Time business hours.

Ideal Experience & Skills

Previous experience in:

  • Sales Development Representative (SDR) roles
  • Business Development Representative (BDR) roles
  • Outbound sales
  • Cold calling
  • Recruiting
  • Lead generation

Additional experience:

  • Experience using CRM systems or applicant tracking systems.
  • Experience working with U.S.-based companies or clients.
  • Experience in commission-based or performance-driven environments.
  • Familiarity with sales metrics and pipeline management.
  • Experience meeting daily activity and conversion goals.

Tech Stack & Tools

  • Google Workspace (Gmail, Sheets, Drive)
  • Slack
  • CRM or Lead Tracking Software
  • Phone & Dialer Systems
  • Email Outreach Tools

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

An SDR’s day is focused on prospecting, qualifying leads, and generating opportunities for the sales team.

You will:

  • Review your lead queue and daily outreach goals.
  • Make outbound calls to prospective candidates and leads.
  • Send follow-up emails and text messages.
  • Conduct qualification conversations.
  • Log notes and update CRM records in real time.
  • Follow established outreach cadences.
  • Coordinate handoffs for qualified prospects.
  • Monitor progress toward daily and weekly performance goals.
  • Participate in team coaching and training sessions.

In essence: you are responsible for creating opportunities, building the top of the sales pipeline, and helping drive business growth through consistent outreach and lead qualification.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Daily outbound call volume.
  • Daily outreach activity completion.
  • Lead qualification rate.
  • Contact-to-conversation conversion rate.
  • Qualified lead generation.
  • Follow-up completion rate.
  • CRM accuracy and activity tracking.
  • Weekly and monthly performance goal attainment.
  • Overall contribution to pipeline growth.

Why Join Us?

  • Fully remote work environment.
  • Opportunity to develop and grow your sales career.
  • Ongoing coaching and professional development.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • Exposure to a variety of sales campaigns and industries.
  • Clear opportunities for advancement as the company grows.
  • Access to modern tools and systems that support success and productivity.

What Happens After You Apply

Right after you apply, you’ll receive an email invitation from Spark Hire to record your Intro Video. It’s a short, self-recorded video, completed once on your own time, and it’s the final step that completes your application.

Here’s why we do it this way. Instead of repeating yourself on screening call after screening call, you tell your story once and it carries forward. Hiring managers get to see how you actually communicate before you meet, so when you’re a fit, the first conversation isn’t starting from scratch. Fewer interviews, and the ones you do have count for more.

Don’t overthink it. Record it as many times as you like—nobody sees the takes you discard. Just be yourself. Your Intro Video invitation will come from Spark Hire, our trusted video interview platform, so please keep an eye on both your inbox and spam folder for the email.

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application Review
  2. Intro Video
  3. Client Interview
  4. Offer & Onboarding

Job Details:

About the Role

Constellation Payments is seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Risk Analyst to support merchant risk monitoring, transaction review, bank account change controls, and ongoing portfolio risk oversight. This role is responsible for identifying and mitigating emerging fraud, compliance, transaction, chargeback, ACH, NACHA, website, MCC, and merchant behavior risks across both new and existing merchants.

The ideal candidate is proactive, analytical, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where priorities, workloads, risk trends, and business needs continuously evolve. They are comfortable managing multiple investigations simultaneously, making sound risk-based decisions, and taking ownership of issues through to resolution. Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, the ability to adapt quickly to changing processes and priorities, and a willingness to take initiative beyond day-to-day responsibilities.

The Risk Analyst will work closely with Risk leadership, Underwriting, Onboarding, Merchant Support, Finance, Compliance, and external partners to ensure risk items are identified, investigated, documented, escalated, and resolved in a timely and consistent manner. This role plays a critical part in strengthening post-boarding controls, protecting the merchant portfolio, supporting regulatory compliance, and driving continuous improvement across risk operations.

This position offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact within a growing organization, contributing to the development of risk programs, monitoring frameworks, operational controls, and strategic initiatives while supporting the evolving needs of the business.


Compensation & Role Details:

Expected Salary Range: The expected base salary range for this role is between $55,000 to 62,000 CAD, depending on experience and qualifications

Role Type: New Role

AI Disclosure: AI may be used during the hiring process.


What You’ll Do

  • Monitor merchant activity for fraud, compliance, reputational, operational, ACH, chargeback, and transaction-related risks, investigating flagged activity including held transactions, large tickets, refunds, duplicate transactions, excessive authorizations/declines, suspicious processing behavior, and emerging risk trends.

  • Take ownership of new responsibilities, support cross-functional projects, and perform miscellaneous duties assigned by management to meet evolving organizational needs.

  • Working understanding of payment processing workflows, merchant accounts, transaction monitoring, chargebacks, ACH returns, refunds, and risk flags.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to validate documentation, identify inconsistencies, and maintain accurate case notes and trackers.
  • Ability to manage multiple open reviews, follow-ups, escalations, and time-sensitive cases at once.
  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to communicate clearly with partners, merchants, and internal stakeholders.
  • Comfort working with CRM/case management tools, spreadsheets, and operational trackers.
  • Ability to follow documented procedures while identifying gaps, control weaknesses, or opportunities for process improvement.
  • Sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling sensitive merchant, banking, fraud, and compliance information.
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with Risk, Underwriting, Onboarding, Merchant Support, Finance, Product, and partner-facing teams.
  • Working knowledge of ACH processing, NACHA Operating Rules, ACH return codes, unauthorized return thresholds, administrative returns, and ACH risk monitoring best practices.
  • Ability to review and investigate ACH-related risk indicators, including unusual return activity, account validation concerns, transaction anomalies, and merchant processing trends.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in merchant acquiring, PayFac operations, fintech, payment risk, card-not-present environments, or payment gateway operations.
  • Familiarity with Payrix, Salesforce, Zift, Vantiv IQ, LegitScript, GIACT, Inscribe, or similar risk and verification tools.
  • Experience reviewing bank change documentation, voided checks, bank letters, authorized signers, ownership matches, or account verification controls.

  • Knowledge of MCC risk classification, high-risk industries, NEC classifications, prohibited merchant categories, and enhanced due diligence triggers.
  • Experience preparing risk reporting, KPI summaries, audit support documentation, or operational leadership updates.
  • Comfort working in a remote-first environment with strong follow-through, documentation discipline, and queue ownership.
  • Experience working with ACH risk monitoring programs, NACHA compliance requirements, return rate management, and payment network rules.

Key Success Measures

  • Risk queues, held transactions, bank changes, alerts, and follow-ups are reviewed consistently and within expected operating cadence.
  • Cases and monitoring logs are accurate, complete, and updated with clear next steps, owner, and status.
  • High-risk, critical, or suspicious activity is escalated promptly with supporting detail.

Work Location & Flexibility

Who We Are 

Marketbridge is a leading integrated growth consulting and marketing services firm that accelerates performance from strategy through execution. We combine management consultancy with marketing agency expertise, all backed by marketing science, creative problem-solving, and technological know-how. Our integrated approach brings together teams, technology, data, strategies, processes, and plans to fuel sustainable revenue growth and build deeper, more resonant customer relationships. With a team of 300 professionals across global locations including Boston, D.C.,London, and Canada, Marketbridge partners with over 150 clients worldwide, including Amazon Web Services, AMD, MetLife, Flex and CERN.

 

Who We're Looking For

Marketbridge is seeking a Director, Marketing Analytics to lead the strategy, design, and evolution of the data and analytics capabilities that power modern marketing programs.

This role sits at the intersection of marketing strategy, marketing technology, data operations, measurement, and business intelligence. The Director will help clients establish the connected data foundations required to activate audiences effectively, measure marketing performance accurately, and turn complex information into actionable business insight.

The ideal candidate is equally comfortable discussing marketing objectives with senior client stakeholders and working with technical teams to implement and configure tracking and tagging mechanisms, design the data architectures, build data integrations and workflows, and establish governance standards.

This leader will oversee a team responsible for transforming, integrating, automating, and analyzing marketing data across complex client ecosystems. They will partner closely with Marketing Technology, Marketing Operations, Demand Strategy, Media, and client teams to ensure data moves reliably from source systems through activation and measurement.

Success in this role requires a combination of data strategy, technical fluency, analytical thinking, client leadership, and people development, along with the ability to translate between technical requirements and business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead marketing data strategy and architecture across complex client environments, defining how data should be captured, integrated, transformed, governed, activated, and measured across marketing ecosystems.

  • Collaborate with Marketing Technology & Operations leadership to establish reusable methodologies, standards, and intellectual property for data architecture, integration, data quality, automation, measurement readiness, and analytics delivery.

  • Own the design and governance of scalable marketing data solutions spanning CRM, marketing automation platforms, media and ABM platforms, web analytics, data warehouses, BI environments, and other marketing and sales systems.

  • Oversee data integration and transformation frameworks, including ETL processes, APIs, cloud connectors, workflow automation, SQL- and Python-based solutions, and other methods used to move and prepare data across platforms.

  • Establish data quality and governance standards that improve the accuracy, consistency, accessibility, security, and reliability of marketing data and downstream reporting.

  • Advance marketing measurement and analytics capabilities by partnering with Strategy, Media, and Marketing Technology & Operations teams to establish reliable data foundations, KPI frameworks, reporting structures, and analytical approaches.

  • Connect data to business insight, helping client and internal teams understand how data infrastructure, measurement, and analytical outputs can improve marketing decisions and business outcomes.

  • Serve as a senior trusted advisor to clients, including Marketing Operations, Analytics, Technology, and Marketing leaders, on data architecture, operational data strategy, measurement readiness, governance, and future-state capabilities.

  • Lead complex discovery and solution-design engagements, facilitating stakeholder conversations, documenting requirements, identifying gaps, and developing future-state recommendations and implementation roadmaps.

  • Evaluate emerging data, analytics, automation, and AI capabilities, identifying opportunities to increase efficiency, improve decision-making, and expand Marketbridge's client offerings.

  • Lead and develop Marketing Data & Analytics talent, providing coaching, technical guidance, performance management, career development, and opportunities for team members to expand their skills.

  • Guide team resourcing and delivery quality across multiple client engagements, ensuring work is appropriately staffed and delivered against established technical and analytical standards.

  • Support new business and organic growth, leading data and analytics discovery, solution design, technical scoping, estimation, proposal development, and client presentations.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in marketing data, marketing analytics, data engineering, marketing operations, marketing technology, business intelligence, or a closely related discipline, ideally within an agency, consulting, or complex client-service environment.

  • Demonstrated experience leading marketing data strategy and solution architecture across interconnected marketing and sales technology environments.

  • Strong understanding of the role data plays across the marketing lifecycle, including audience development, segmentation, personalization, campaign activation, measurement, attribution, reporting, and optimization.

  • Experience designing or overseeing ETL/ELT processes, data transformations, automated workflows, APIs, system integrations, and data quality frameworks.

  • Strong working knowledge of SQL and familiarity with Python and modern data transformation or automation approaches; the Director does not need to be the primary hands-on developer but must be technically fluent enough to guide solutions and challenge architectural decisions.

  • Deep expertise in web analytics and tag management strategy and implementation, including GA4, GTM, and Adobe Analytics, with experience defining measurement frameworks, tagging and data layer architectures, event taxonomies, implementation standards, QA processes, and governance across enterprise digital properties.

  • Experience working across platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, 6sense, Demandbase, cloud data warehouses, BI platforms, and data integration/automation tools.

  • Strong understanding of data architecture, data modeling, governance, identity, integration patterns, and marketing data quality.

  • Experience with marketing measurement and analytics, including the ability to connect campaign and customer data to KPIs, reporting, performance analysis, and business outcomes.

  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strong client-facing communication and executive presentation skills, with experience advising senior marketing, operations, analytics, and technology stakeholders.

  • Proven ability to lead ambiguous and complex engagements from discovery and requirements gathering through solution design, implementation, and optimization.

  • Experience managing and developing multidisciplinary data and analytics talent, including coaching individual contributors and emerging people leaders.

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. We manage services for individuals with serious mental health needs, substance use disorders, traumatic brain injuries, and intellectual/development (IDD) disabilities. Our mission is to help individuals and families build strong foundations for healthy, fulfilling lives.

Why Work for Us?

Trillium believes that empowering others begins with supporting our team. We offer our employees:

  • A collaborative, mission-driven work environment
  • Competitive benefits and work-from-home options for most positions
  • Opportunities for professional growth in a diverse inclusive culture

Every day, our work changes lives – from children thriving through early intervention and school-based therapies, to adults with severe mental illness living independently and contributing to their communities.

If you are looking for a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact on the lives of others, apply today!

What We’re Looking For

Trillium Health Resources has a career opening for a Care Transitions Care Manager to join our team! The Care Transitions Care Manager is responsible for providing in reach and transition care management to members residing in institutional, congregate, or facility-based settings, including ACH’s), hospitals, inpatient units, and other qualifying settings. The Care Transitions Care Manager educates members and guardians about how to effectively navigate the physical, behavioral, and social service systems for themselves and about the existence of informal/community resources available to them; and facilitates the member/guardian access to these resources. The Care Transitions Care Manager provides care planning with foundations in national evidence based and informed standards for whole person care. The Care Transitions Care Manager provides guidance and monitoring to providers regarding social determinant needs, medical needs, and other needs of the member. The Care Transitions Care Manager completes required documentation, paperwork, and tasks in Trillium’s software platform in accordance with designated timeframes. The Care Transitions Care Manager works on an interdisciplinary team to address the functions of the Olmstead Settlement and Tailored Plan. The Care Transitions Care Manager is expected to assess and monitor the member’s health and safety, including when the Trillium Catchment is under a state of emergency or weather advisory.

On a typical day, you might:

  • Provide age- and developmentally appropriate education for the member and the member’s family members and/or guardians about the opportunity to receive care in a more integrated community-based setting and available services in such settings.
  • Provide complex care management, in compliance with NCQA and any other identified regulatory/required accreditation standards, to assigned members who may have identified needs with behavioral health, physical health, co-occurring, co-morbid or multi-morbid conditions.
  • Provide the member and/or the member’s family members or guardians opportunities to meet with other individuals with SMI/SPMI diagnoses who are living, working, and receiving services in a community setting.
  • Identify, document, and attempt to address barriers to relocation to a more integrated community setting.
  • Engage members who are residing in such as State Psychiatric Hospitals, ACH to provide education about permanent supportive housing, supports, services, and other community resources.

Employee Benefits:

Trillium knows that work/life balance is essential. That’s why we offer:

  • Typical working hours: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm; flexible work schedules with some roles with management approval.
  • Work-from-home options available for most positions
  • Health Insurance with no premium for employee coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 24 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) plus 12 paid holidays in your first year
  • NC Local Government Retirement Pension (defined-benefit plan)
  • 401k with 5% employer match and immediate vesting
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) qualifying employer
  • Quarterly stipend for remote work supplies

Qualifications

Required:

  • Must meet QP status.
  • Fully licensed by the NC governing board regulating Human Services professions; OR
  • Fully licensed RN who is licensed to practice in the state of NC by the NC Board of Nursing who also has four (4) years of full-time experience with the MH/DD/SA population served; OR
  • A graduate of a college or university with a Master’s degree in a human service field and has one year of full-time, pre or post-graduate degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has one year of full-time, pre or postgraduate degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling; OR
  • A graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a human service field and has two years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has two years of full-time, pre or post bachelor's degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling; OR
  • A graduate of a college or university with a bachelor's degree in a field other than human services and has four years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated MH/DD/SA experience with the MH/DD/SA population, or a substance abuse professional who has four years of full-time, pre or post-bachelor's degree accumulated supervised experience in alcoholism and drug abuse counseling.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Must reside within Trillium’s Mid State Region, which includes the following counties: Anson, Guilford, Montgomery, Randolph, and Richmond.
  • Must be able to travel within catchment as required.

Preferred:

  • License and/or certification may be accepted as noted above.

Deadline for Application:Monday August 24, 2026, at 11:59PM

How to Apply

To be considered, submit your application and resume through our ADP Career Center. Your resume must include:

  • Employer name, dates of service (month/year), average hours worked per week, and essential job duties
  • Education details (degree type, date awarded, institution, field of study)
  • Licensure/certification information, if applicable

After submission, your resume will be reviewed to ensure it meets the essential criteria for the position. You’ll be notified by HR regarding your application status as appropriate. All applicants will receive a final update once the recruitment cycle closes.

Join our Talent Community through ADP to stay informed about future opportunities. Be sure to keep your resume updated in your profile.

Trillium Health Resources is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer and a drug-free workplace. All candidates must pass a drug test as a condition of employment.

jobs.excerpt: Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
jobs.description:
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.

Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora,你好, hallo, vítejte!

Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.

What you'd be doing in this role:

Canva is making experimentation a much bigger part of how we build and ship product.

At our scale, shipping changes and watching what happens isn't enough. Teams need to know whether a change actually improved the product and catch changes that unexpectedly hurt important guardrails such as retention or application performance.

This Staff Software Engineer will provide senior technical leadership across the backend systems behind Canva's experimentation programme.

You'll help evolve the platform teams use to set up experiments, target users, expose variants and measure outcomes in the safest and most intuitive way possible. We're moving towards a platform that does more than report results. It should reinforce good experimentation practices, surface signals faster and alert early when things go wrong.

With the advent of AI, we’re also looking at how we can automate more of the analysis process to help our teams learn faster and iterate.

You'll take ownership of significant technical problems, work with senior leaders across Canva and help shape where the platform should go next by working with the teams building the platform.

You’re probably a match:

We'd love to hear from you if you fit one or more of these. You don't need to meet all of them, but the more the better and if you join the team, we're invested in helping you grow.

Experience:

  • Backend platform engineering: You've built backend systems or platforms that other engineers depend on, and understand what changes when your software becomes part of somebody else's critical path.

  • Experimentation exposure at scale: You've built, operated or worked deeply with experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or progressive-rollout systems in a large engineering environment.

  • Technical leadership: You've taken ambiguous engineering problems, formed a technical direction and helped other engineers move towards an outcome.

  • Driving adoption: You've built internal platforms or capabilities and understand that the technology only succeeds when other teams trust and use it.

Technical knowledge:

  • Backend and distributed systems: Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience designing reliable backend systems and reasoning about scalability, availability, consistency and failure modes.

  • Data systems: Enough familiarity with data engineering, analytics engineering or large-scale data processing to understand how experimentation data is generated, moved and consumed.

  • Experimentation concepts: Familiarity with experiment assignment, targeting, variants, feature flags, metrics, guardrails and progressive rollout.

  • Language depth: Java is our primary language and would be useful, but it isn't a hard requirement. At Staff level, we're more interested in strong engineering fundamentals and your ability to transfer them between languages.

Nice to haves:

  • You've built this before: Direct experience designing or building experimentation, A/B testing, feature-management or rollout infrastructure — either inside a large technology company or for a platform vendor.

  • Data crossover: A background spanning software engineering and data science, data engineering or analytics engineering.

  • Feature flags: Experience building feature flagging, user targeting, progressive rollout or automated guardrail systems.

  • Statistical intuition: You don't need to be a data scientist, but being comfortable enough with experimentation and statistics to work closely with one will be valuable.

About the Group & Team:

This role sits within Rollout Insights, the subgroup responsible for experimentation at Canva.

The team builds shared experimentation capabilities used across the company.

Engineers use the platform to configure and launch experiments. Data scientists use the resulting data to understand impact. Product teams use those insights to decide what should roll out, change or stop.

The team already brings together software engineering and senior data science expertise, which matters because the hardest problems sit across both disciplines.

You'll also collaborate broadly across Canva's engineering and data science organisations, including with senior technical leaders who depend on the platform.

Experimentation is now a major company priority, so demand for the team's capabilities is growing quickly. There's already a platform to build from, with plenty of important technical work still ahead.

What's in it for you?

Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.

Here's a taste of what's on offer:

  • Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
  • Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
  • An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
  • Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally

Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Other stuff to know

We see AI as a powerful amplifier of creativity and technology at Canva. We're evolving how we assess AI skills in our Technology hiring experience — you'll tackle interactive, real-time challenges that reflect the kind of work we do. In some interviews, you may also be asked to solve a problem using an AI tool to show how you approach challenges with tech by your side.

We make hiring decisions based on your experience, skills and passion, as well as how you can enhance Canva and our culture.

When you apply, please tell us the pronouns you use and any reasonable adjustments you may need during the interview process. We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva, so even if you don't feel like your skills quite match what's listed above — we still want to hear from you!

Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.

Where and how you can work

Our flagship campus is in Sydney, with a second campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth, & Adelaide. You have flexibility in how and where you work — whether that's from one of our spaces, from home, or a mix of both. This role is remote-friendly within Australia, so you can choose the setup that empowers you and your team to do your best work.

In partnership with one of the largest financial conglomerates, we are creating a secure, transparent, and high-performance trading infrastructure that can support institutional volumes while remaining accessible to retail participants. Position Overview

You already have strong, specific opinions about how Hyperliquid, Aster, dydx, and Drift have made their product choices. You follow the design space — funding mechanisms, oracle construction, ADL versus insurance-fund tradeoffs, cross- versus isolated-margin accounting — closely enough to argue for a position, not just summarize what others have shipped. We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Trading with deep, hands-on experience shipping product at an orderbook trading venue to work on Strium – a DeFi L1 blockchain with an on-chain orderbook exchange. You will own a core surface of the exchange — order types and margin, the programmatic / API trading surface, or listings and risk parameters — and ship its v1 in partnership with engineering, risk, and our market making partners.

You will operate as the primary product interface to market makers and high-volume traders, translating their requirements into specifications that engineering can build against, and pushing back when the right answer for the venue differs from the loudest voice. You will define how we measure ourselves against similar products such as Hyperliquid, Aster, dydx, and the DEXs that matter, and run honest reviews against those benchmarks.

This role offers an opportunity to shape the product direction of our exchange at an early stage, working alongside a distributed team of engineers and traders building next-generation financial infrastructure. You will start by shipping v1 of your core surface, and over time help expand the venue's surface area into adjacent territory — lending markets, hedging and basis-trade flows, structured surfaces — as the product matures. The role reports to the Head of Product.

Why this role matters

You will own a core surface of Strium and ship its v1. The decisions you make in the first 90 days set the bar for how the venue behaves under real volume. You will be the product voice that market makers, traders, and engineers align around. If that is the work you have been looking for, this is the chair.

Team and stakeholders

  • Reports to the Head of Product.
  • Daily collaboration with engineering, risk, and our market making partners.
  • Frequent engagement with institutional counterparties.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the product strategy and v1 spec for a core trading surface — order types and margining, the programmatic / API surface, or listings and risk parameters. The specific surface will be aligned in the first week.
  • Act as the primary product interface to market makers and high-volume traders, turning their input into spec and maintaining a coherent product direction across competing requests.
  • Drive the listings pipeline end-to-end:
    • Define which markets to list, on what timeline, and against which benchmark venues.
    • Set initial market parameters: leverage caps, tick / lot size, funding cap, oracle source, margin requirements.
    • Coordinate engineering, risk, and MM readiness for each launch.
  • Partner with engineering on the matching engine, risk engine, and API contracts, contributing to spec reviews and design decisions such as ADL versus insurance-fund design, cross- versus isolated-margin accounting, and oracle integration.
  • Define and track product success metrics — depth, slippage, fill rate, API latency, listings velocity, MM uptime etc.
  • Build and maintain the competitive intelligence function for the exchange: deeply understand what competitor venues have shipped, what they got right, and where the open ground is.
  • Write the specs, RFCs, and MM briefs that align engineering, risk, and external partners. Pre-product is a writing-heavy role.
  • Act as the primary product interface to institutional and incumbent-finance counterparties, translating their requirements into specifications and maintaining a coherent venue direction across these stakeholders.
  • Beyond v1 of your initial surface, contribute to the design of adjacent surfaces — lending markets, hedging and basis-trade flows, structured surfaces — and seed the groundwork during early shipping so future expansion is not a rewrite.

Requirements

Must have

Exchange Product Experience

  • 5–8 years of product management experience, with 2+ years shipping product at an orderbook trading venue (derivatives, CEX or DEX).
    • You worked on the trading or exchange team.
    • You have owned a roadmap with market makers and institutional traders as a real stakeholder.

Trading Literacy

  • Fluent in trader vocabulary: funding, basis, skew, taker / maker, ADL, oracle slippage, latency-sensitive flow.
  • Familiarity with the operational mechanics of perp markets — liquidation engines, insurance funds, cross- and isolated-margin, funding rate design, mark price construction.
  • Strong, specific opinions about other DEXs' product choices: what they got right, what's still open, and what you would do differently.
  • You actively trade perps with non-trivial volume.

Product Craft in Ambiguity

  • Track record of shipping in pre-PMF environments. You can define your own surface and scope rather than executing against an inherited roadmap.
  • Comfortable making decisions without a research team behind you.

Communication & Writing

  • Excellent written communication. Your specs, RFCs, and memos align people without requiring meetings.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with both engineers and external trading partners, in their own register.
  • Japanese language proficiency is preferred but not required, given regular engagement with Japanese partners and counterparties.

Technical Fluency

  • Technical enough that engineers respect you in design review.
  • Comfortable reading code and understanding what's happening under the hood.

Strong Plus

New Venue Launch

  • You have launched a new orderbook trading venue from zero.

Quant or Trading Background

  • You have done quant, market-making, or trading work yourself, in a professional or serious personal capacity.

Onchain Risk Infrastructure

  • Experience with oracle design, liquidation auctions, or cross-margin accounting on-chain.

Asia Market Context

  • Familiarity with Japanese or APAC capital markets, retail trading culture, or institutional trading workflows.
  • Lending Protocols
  • Familiarity with the design space of on-chain lending and money markets (Aave, Morpho, Drift's lending surface, etc.) and how they interact with leveraged trading.
  • Hedging & Structured Products
  • Experience with hedging desks, basis-trade flows, or structured products from traditional finance or crypto.
  • Incumbent Finance Product Experience
  • You have shipped product inside or alongside an incumbent financial institution — a broker-dealer, prime broker, established exchange, or asset manager — and understand how they evaluate, integrate, and operate trading venues.

Location

Preferred Location: Tokyo or Singapore
Alternative Locations: Hong Kong, Seoul, or Taiwan

Compensation and benefits

Compensation aligned with our Global Salary Standard plus equity. Benefits include:

  • Unlimited time off.
  • Stock options.
  • Annual workations (most recent: Seoul, Tokyo, Croatia, Turkey, Belgium).
  • Premium tooling from machine to AI agents.

Why Join Us

  • Shape the product – a DeFi L1 chain powered by an orderbook perp DEX – that aims to bring TradFi on-chain, in partnership with one of Japan's largest financial conglomerates.
  • Operate with great autonomy and influence the architecture of trading infrastructure at the earliest stage.
  • Collaborate with a world-class, distributed engineering team building purpose-designed exchange infrastructure.
  • Competitive compensation, with equity / stock options available when conditions are met.
  • Remote, with overlap with APAC working hours. Hybrid in Tokyo or Singapore preferred.
  • Growth opportunities in a rapidly evolving space.

  • Experienced in provider enrollment, payer contracting, credentialing, or healthcare administrative operations
  • Comfortable serving as the primary point of contact while maintaining professionalism, responsiveness, and accuracy
  • Strong project management and workflow coordination skills with the ability to work independently in a remote environment
  • Detail-oriented with exceptional follow-through and documentation habits
  • Able to balance relationship management with hands-on execution and task completion
  • Comfortable working within a billable-time structure and tracking work accurately
  • Experienced in provider-side healthcare operations, consulting, MSO, RCM, credentialing, or enrollment services environments rather than exclusively payer-side settings
  • Motivated by operational excellence, service, organization, accountability, and relationship building

The Account Manager is responsible for managing a portfolio of healthcare accounts and overseeing provider enrollment, payer contracting, credentialing, recredentialing, and related operational workflows. This individual serves as the primary point of contact for assigned accounts and is responsible for managing projects, maintaining timelines, resolving payer issues, coordinating documentation, and personally completing the work necessary to support successful outcomes.

This is a fully hands-on role with no direct reports or people management responsibilities. The Account Manager will independently maintain relationships, oversee workflow visibility, coordinate deliverables, and execute provider enrollment and contracting tasks directly. Success in this position requires exceptional organization, communication, follow-through, and the ability to manage multiple active accounts simultaneously while maintaining accuracy, responsiveness, and a high level of service.
